repo.description: Self-hosted Shadow AI discovery and governance. Evidence-first visibility across network, endpoints, Active Directory and Entra ID.
repo.name: open-shadow-ai

pull_request.body:
Production installation needs bounded admission, recoverable queues, reliable readiness signals and evidence tied to the images actually deployed. This change implements those controls and adds an isolated qualification lab with measurable failure and restoration scenarios.

- Bound SSO state creation and provider calls; fail closed when admission cannot be verified.
- Enforce queue capacity and reference accounting, retain unacknowledged/dead-letter data, and provide controlled replay, reconciliation and archival garbage collection. Preserve delivery of older agent batches.
- Add worker progress probes, operational alerts and physical resource measurements.
- Lock dependencies and build inputs; verify complete OCI evidence and scan the actual runtime inventory on both architectures. Maintain four service-image recipes with pinned Go/source/module/APK inputs. Main-branch attestation covers verified archives; no registry publication is introduced.
- Add labeled detection evaluation, load/fault/pressure/probe exercises, cold restoration and guarded disposable-resource cleanup. Read-only Kubernetes rendering and IdP checks expose their qualification limits.

The OCI scanner uses byte-identical private layouts with verified blob hashes and unchanged-snapshot checks. Temporary containers retain name/image evidence across journal resumes. A bounded, secret-safe worker diagnostic preserves the original installation failure code.

Independent local verification: 245 image/scanner tests, 196 qualification tests and 99 diagnostic/monitoring tests passed. Eight POSIX cases require Linux and one Promtool test requires the real tool; mandatory hosted checks cover these execution environments. Twelve official image indexes and both architecture manifests were independently verified. Ruff and workflow validation passed.

Hosted native builds, APK signature checks, all 18 image scans and actual Compose/pressure/restoration exercises are required before accepting this PR. Local results do not establish their success.

Documentation: [delivery](https://github.com/alebgl77/open-shadow-ai/blob/codex/production-hardening-lots/docs/production-delivery.md), [qualification](https://github.com/alebgl77/open-shadow-ai/blob/codex/production-hardening-lots/docs/production-qualification.md), [worker diagnostics](https://github.com/alebgl77/open-shadow-ai/blob/codex/production-hardening-lots/docs/worker-diagnostics.md).

Deployment remains one organization per installation with external stores for the Kubernetes profile. Real IdP/MFA, AD fleet, Kubernetes HA, representative detection accuracy and production sizing/RPO/RTO still require the target environment. Browser-based IdP execution fails closed until containment is supported. The bounded frontend parser mitigation remains documented; a clean named-package audit does not imply physical parser removal.

source_inputs.deploy/service-builds/Dockerfile.node-ex:
# Maintained recipe 1: pinned release source, toolchain and readonly module graph.
FROM golang:1.26.6-alpine3.24@sha256:3889b425f035be855a72fb4755265311293b6d414521f0a519d819df32222d83 AS build
WORKDIR /src
ENV CGO_ENABLED=0 GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOENV=off GOWORK=off GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly GOTELEMETRY=off
RUN test "$(go version | cut -d ' ' -f 3)" = go1.26.6 \
    && wget -O /tmp/source.tar.gz https://codeload.github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/tar.gz/6044da783597cc3b57aef7580ddcdcff58a4ee99 \
    && echo 'cfec7478aa9bfd011f29df084584b7c7b68dfef85a24d28e9d6d5f88224f83c3  /tmp/source.tar.gz' | sha256sum -c - \
    && tar -xzf /tmp/source.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /src \
    && rm /tmp/source.tar.gz
COPY requirements/service-builds/node-exporter/go.mod requirements/service-builds/node-exporter/go.sum ./
COPY requirements/service-builds/node-exporter/modules.txt /locked-modules.txt
RUN printf '%s\n' '261fad93f8f76ebdce7317674fd68256f95e59f6cb435ca1cd351083ac8f65bb  go.mod' 'f8e510431472d38ed55d0a2e3d7839a0d2a78fe591e0c41e78205dbf6b8f02c0  go.sum' '45df7e15ac5939a832aa9bfcc3e488ca8cbb69c8c28b2fc766e2d0ef59e16d54  /locked-modules.txt' | sha256sum -c - \
    && go mod download \
    && go mod verify \
    && go list -m all | cmp - /locked-modules.txt \
    && mkdir /out \
    && go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags='-s -w -X github.com/prometheus/common/version.Version=1.12.1-shadai.1 -X github.com/prometheus/common/version.Revision=6044da783597cc3b57aef7580ddcdcff58a4ee99 -X github.com/prometheus/common/version.Branch=maintained -X github.com/prometheus/common/version.BuildUser=shadai -X github.com/prometheus/common/version.BuildDate=2026-10-06T00:00:00Z' -o /out/node_exporter . \
    && cp /locked-modules.txt /out/GO-MODULES.txt \
    && find /go/pkg/mod -type f \( -iname 'license*' -o -iname 'notice*' -o -iname 'copying*' -o -iname 'copyright*' \) \
       -exec sh -c 'for p do printf "\nSOURCE LICENSE %s\n" "$p"; cat "$p"; done' sh {} + > /out/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt
FROM quay.io/prometheus/node-exporter:v1.12.1@sha256:1b4e4438faca4dd7e001dd445d161a4a2091b0fededa84093b3a8dfeae1f1be0
COPY --from=build /out/node_exporter /bin/node_exporter
COPY --from=build /src/LICENSE /usr/local/share/licenses/shadai/node-exporter/LICENSE
COPY --from=build /usr/local/go/LICENSE /usr/local/share/licenses/shadai/node-exporter/GO-LICENSE
COPY --from=build /out/GO-MODULES.txt /out/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt /usr/local/share/licenses/shadai/node-exporter/
LABEL io.shadai.maintenance.recipe="1" \
      io.shadai.maintenance.component="node-exporter" \
      io.shadai.maintenance.version="v1.12.1-shadai.1" \
      io.shadai.maintenance.source="6044da783597cc3b57aef7580ddcdcff58a4ee99" \
      io.shadai.maintenance.toolchain="go1.26.6"
RUN /bin/node_exporter --version

Vulnerabilities.Title: The golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package is unmaintained, unsafe by design, and has known security issues
Vulnerabilities.Description:
The golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package is unsafe by design, has numerous known security issues, is not maintained, and should not be used.

If you are required to interoperate with OpenPGP systems and need a maintained package, consider github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto/openpgp which is a maintained fork that aims to be a drop-in replacement for this package.
